now.accept: Feature set maps only to those items (install/update/self-update/schedule/newproj/config); none of the ACFS VPS machinery is present.
now.text: Minimal scope: install tools, set up the macOS terminal environment, install a weekly-update plist, manual update via CLI, self-update, plus the explicitly requested project bootstrap (macacfs newproj, ported from acfs newproj, with optional GitHub publish and ru registration) and a small persistent settings store (macacfs config). Still not a full ACFS port (no user provisioning, OS upgrade, service orchestration, phase runner).

now.accept: Simulated failure states drive the schedule: fail->nightly; 3 fails->2pm daily; success->back to weekly.
now.text: If a scheduled run fails, retry nightly (03:00) until success; once 3 consecutive scheduled runs have failed, switch to daily 2pm attempts until success, then return to weekly.

now.accept: Each manifest row names exactly one of brew, installer-sh, cargo-git, go; the dispatcher handles those four and fails loud on any other method; installing a sample of each method the catalog uses (brew, installer-sh, cargo-git) succeeds on the Mac.
now.text: Per-tool install/update dispatch across 4 methods: brew (Homebrew tap formula, install-or-upgrade), installer-sh (the repo's own installer via curl|bash, with optional flags), cargo-git (cargo install --git --force), and go (go install <module>@latest).

prev.accept: Manifest row per tool names its method; installing a sample of each method type succeeds on the Mac.
prev.text: Per-tool install/update dispatch across ~5 methods: own install.sh (curl|bash), Homebrew tap, cargo install --git, go install/Makefile, npm/bash.

now.accept: The 15 tap-formula tools (NTM, MAIL, UBS, BV, CASS, CM, SLB, DCG, BR, CAAM, RU, RCH, XF, TRU, EE) use the brew method with a dicklesworthstone/tap/<formula> ref and install/update through brew; no tool with a tap formula uses a non-brew method.
now.text: Prefer Homebrew wherever dicklesworthstone/tap publishes a formula for a tool; tools with no tap formula (e.g. MS via cargo-git, SRPS via its installer-sh) use their own method.

prev.accept: MS and SRPS rows use the brew method; install/update go through brew for them.
prev.text: Prefer Homebrew where a tool publishes a tap/formula (e.g. MS, SRPS).

now.accept: On a Mac missing e.g. go, running macacfs installs go before the tools that need it; gate reports what it installed.
now.text: Prerequisite gate checks for the toolchains the selected tools need (Homebrew, git, rust/cargo, go, uv, node, plus minisign and flock for installers that verify or serialize with them; curl is assumed from macOS) and INSTALLS any that are missing, not just reports them.

now.accept: Running a full 'macacfs install' (no TOOL args) installs omz/p10k/plugins/font, the brew CLI bundle, the tmux config (~/.tmux.conf, prior file backed up), and atuin(+shim)/zoxide/lazygit/ast-grep; ~/.zshrc becomes a managed loader with the prior file backed up; 'macacfs install TOOL...' skips shell setup; --dry-run performs no installs; a full 'macacfs update' brew-upgrades the bundle, font, zoxide, lazygit, ast-grep and atuin.
now.text: Set up the macOS terminal environment to ACFS parity: Oh My Zsh + Powerlevel10k + zsh plugins + a mac-adapted managed zshrc (backing up any existing one) + a Nerd Font, a modern-CLI Homebrew bundle, a tmux config (installed to ~/.tmux.conf, backing up any existing one), and standalone tools (atuin with an agent-safe shim, zoxide, lazygit, ast-grep), performed as part of a full 'macacfs install' (no tool selectors); a full 'macacfs update' also refreshes the Homebrew bundle and the brew-installed standalone tools without rewriting shell config.
